clue: Tokyo, Japan 🇯🇵
fact: Japan's capital is the world's most populous metropolitan area, sprawled across 23 special wards on Honshu.

clue: Paris, France 🇫🇷
fact: France's capital grew outward from the Île de la Cité and is ringed by the boulevards of Haussmann.

clue: Cairo, Egypt 🇪🇬
fact: Egypt's capital and the largest city in the Arab world, sitting on the banks of the Nile.

clue: Sydney, Australia 🇦🇺
fact: Australia's most populous city is built around the drowned river valley of Port Jackson.

clue: Rio de Janeiro, Brazil 🇧🇷
fact: Brazil's capital until 1960, it sits in a granite bay ringed by steep forested peaks.

clue: Nairobi, Kenya 🇰🇪
fact: Kenya's capital was founded as a railway depot in 1899 and has a national park on its doorstep.

clue: Reykjavik, Iceland 🇮🇸
fact: The world's most northern capital city, heated by geothermal water that arrives almost entirely free.

clue: Cape Town, South Africa 🇿🇦
fact: One of South Africa's three capitals, set between Table Mountain and two meeting oceans.

clue: New York City, United States 🇺🇸
fact: The most populous city in the United States, fused from five boroughs at the mouth of the Hudson.

clue: Mumbai, India 🇮🇳
fact: India's port city, formerly Bombay, grew out of seven islands joined together in the 19th century.

clue: Where did the Titanic sink in 1912?
fact: The liner struck an iceberg at 2:40 a.m. and came to rest about 3,800 m down, roughly 600 km southeast of Newfoundland.

clue: Where was the Battle of Waterloo fought in 1815?
fact: Napoleon's last battle ended the French advance; the Lion's Mound on the battlefield marks the spot where the Prince of Orange was found wounded.

clue: Where is the Inca citadel of Machu Picchu?
fact: Built for the emperor Pachacuti around 1450, it was abandoned in the 1570s and never found by the Spanish.

clue: Where is Angkor Wat?
fact: The world's largest religious monument was built in the early 12th century by Suryavarman II as a Hindu temple to Vishnu.

clue: Where is Uluru, the giant red rock of central Australia?
fact: This 348-metre sandstone monolith in the Northern Territory is sacred to the Anangu, who have lived around it for tens of thousands of years.

clue: London, United Kingdom 🇬🇧
fact: Britain's capital straddles the Thames and was founded by the Romans as Londinium nearly two thousand years ago.

clue: Rome, Italy 🇮🇹
fact: Italy's capital was built across seven hills and served as the center of an empire that once ringed the Mediterranean.

clue: Beijing, China 🇨🇳
fact: China's capital has been the seat of imperial power for over 800 years, centered on the Forbidden City.

clue: Moscow, Russia 🇷🇺
fact: Russia's capital grew up around the fortified Kremlin on the banks of the Moskva River.

clue: Where does the Statue of Liberty stand?
fact: A gift from France in 1886, the copper statue stands on Liberty Island in New York Harbor and has turned green from oxidation.

clue: Where does the Eiffel Tower stand?
fact: Built in 1889 as a temporary centerpiece for the World's Fair, it was almost torn down in 1909 before radio antennas saved it.

clue: Where is Badaling, the most visited section of the Great Wall?
fact: Built and rebuilt over two thousand years by successive dynasties, the wall's total length across all branches exceeds 21,000 kilometers.

clue: Where do the Great Pyramids of Giza stand?
fact: The Great Pyramid was the tallest man-made structure on Earth for nearly 3,800 years after its completion around 2560 BC.

clue: Berlin, Germany 🇩🇪
fact: Germany's capital was divided by a concrete wall for 28 years until it fell in 1989.

clue: Los Angeles, United States 🇺🇸
fact: Sprawled across Southern California, it's home to the Hollywood film industry and over 80 miles of coastline.

clue: Dubai, United Arab Emirates 🇦🇪
fact: Once a small pearling and fishing town, it now holds the world's tallest building, the Burj Khalifa.

clue: Hong Kong 🇭🇰
fact: This dense harbor city on China's southern coast was a British colony for over 150 years before its 1997 handover.

clue: Singapore 🇸🇬
fact: This city-state at the tip of the Malay Peninsula is also its own sovereign country, one of only a few city-states left in the world.

clue: Barcelona, Spain 🇪🇸
fact: Catalonia's capital is famous for Gaudí's still-unfinished Sagrada Família basilica.

clue: Where would you find the clock tower nicknamed Big Ben?
fact: The nickname technically refers to the Great Bell inside the Elizabeth Tower at the Palace of Westminster.

clue: Where does the statue of Christ the Redeemer overlook a city?
fact: The 30-metre Art Deco statue atop Corcovado mountain took five years to build and was completed in 1931.

clue: Where are the ruins of the Roman Colosseum?
fact: The largest amphitheater ever built could hold up to 80,000 spectators for gladiator contests and public spectacles.

clue: Where do the Niagara Falls thunder between two countries?
fact: More than six million cubic feet of water tumble over the falls every minute at peak flow, straddling the US-Canada border.

clue: Where does the white marble Taj Mahal stand?
fact: Mughal emperor Shah Jahan built it as a mausoleum for his favorite wife, Mumtaz Mahal, who died in childbirth.

clue: Istanbul, Turkey 🇹🇷
fact: The only major city spanning two continents, it was called Constantinople for over a thousand years.

clue: Bangkok, Thailand 🇹🇭
fact: Thailand's capital is laced with canals and crowned by the glittering spires of the Grand Palace.

clue: Mexico City, Mexico 🇲🇽
fact: Built atop the ruins of the Aztec capital Tenochtitlan, it's slowly sinking because it sits on a drained lakebed.

clue: Amsterdam, Netherlands 🇳🇱
fact: Laced with over 100 kilometers of canals, the Dutch capital is built on millions of wooden piles driven into soft soil.

clue: Venice, Italy 🇮🇹
fact: This Italian city has no roads, only canals and footbridges linking its 118 small islands.

clue: Athens, Greece 🇬🇷
fact: Greece's capital has been continuously inhabited for over 3,400 years beneath the Acropolis.

clue: Seoul, South Korea 🇰🇷
fact: South Korea's capital sits on the Han River and is home to roughly a fifth of the country's population.

clue: Toronto, Canada 🇨🇦
fact: Canada's largest city rises beside Lake Ontario and is marked by the CN Tower, once the world's tallest freestanding structure.

clue: Las Vegas, United States 🇺🇸
fact: This Nevada city rose out of the Mojave Desert and became a gambling hub after casinos were legalized in 1931.

clue: Where is the Mayan pyramid city of Chichen Itza?
fact: Twice a year at the equinox, sunlight creates the illusion of a serpent slithering down the steps of its main pyramid.

clue: Where does Japan's tallest and most sacred mountain stand?
fact: This symmetrical volcano last erupted in 1707 and has been climbed as a pilgrimage for centuries.

clue: Where does the prehistoric stone circle of Stonehenge stand?
fact: Built in stages starting around 3000 BC, some of its massive bluestones were hauled from quarries 240 kilometers away in Wales.

clue: Where does the Leaning Tower of Pisa stand?
fact: The tower began tilting during construction in 1173 because its foundation was laid in unstable soil just three meters deep.

clue: Where does the Golden Gate Bridge span?
fact: Painted in 'International Orange' partly so it would be visible through San Francisco Bay's frequent fog, it opened in 1937.

clue: Where is Africa's tallest mountain?
fact: This free-standing volcanic massif in Tanzania rises straight from savanna plains to a snow-capped summit at 5,895 meters.

clue: Where is the South Rim viewpoint of the Grand Canyon?
fact: The canyon exposes nearly two billion years of Earth's geological history in its layered rock walls.

clue: Buenos Aires, Argentina 🇦🇷
fact: Argentina's capital earned the nickname 'Paris of South America' for its European-style boulevards and architecture.

clue: Jerusalem 🇮🇱
fact: This ancient hill city is sacred to Judaism, Christianity, and Islam, all anchored around its walled Old City.

clue: Vienna, Austria 🇦🇹
fact: Once the seat of the Habsburg Empire, this city has topped global liveability rankings for years running.

clue: Prague, Czech Republic 🇨🇿
fact: Nicknamed the 'City of a Hundred Spires,' its medieval Astronomical Clock has run continuously since 1410.

clue: Shanghai, China 🇨🇳
fact: China's largest city sits on the Yangtze River Delta and hosts one of the world's busiest container ports.

clue: Delhi, India 🇮🇳
fact: India's capital territory layers over a thousand years of history, from the ancient Qutb Minar to British colonial New Delhi.

clue: Lagos, Nigeria 🇳🇬
fact: Nigeria's largest city grew up on a lagoon and is now one of the fastest-growing megacities in Africa.

clue: Jakarta, Indonesia 🇮🇩
fact: Indonesia's capital is sinking so fast that the country is building an entirely new capital, Nusantara, on Borneo.

clue: Where does the Zambezi River plunge over Victoria Falls?
fact: Locally called 'Mosi-oa-Tunya,' or 'the smoke that thunders,' it produces a spray visible from 50 kilometers away.

clue: Where is the ancient city of Petra?
fact: Carved directly into rose-colored sandstone cliffs by the Nabataeans, it thrived as a caravan trading hub over 2,000 years ago.

clue: Where does the Great Sphinx keep watch?
fact: Carved from a single limestone outcrop near the Giza pyramids, its missing nose has been gone for over 600 years, long predating the legend blaming Napoleon's cannons.

clue: Where do giant stone moai statues stand watch over the ocean?
fact: The Rapa Nui people carved nearly 900 moai between the 13th and 16th centuries on this remote volcanic island.

clue: Where does a tidal island crowned by an abbey rise from the sea?
fact: At high tide this Normandy island is cut off from the mainland, with waters that can rush in faster than a person can run.

clue: Where does the fairy-tale castle that inspired Disney's Sleeping Beauty Castle stand?
fact: Bavarian King Ludwig II built it in the 1860s as a private retreat and never saw it finished before his death.

clue: Marrakech, Morocco 🇲🇦
fact: This Moroccan city's medina is centered on Jemaa el-Fnaa, a square that transforms into a food market every night.

clue: Havana, Cuba 🇨🇺
fact: Cuba's capital is famous for its 1950s American cars, kept running for decades under a US trade embargo.

clue: Kyoto, Japan 🇯🇵
fact: Japan's imperial capital for over a thousand years, it escaped major bombing in WWII and still holds nearly 1,600 Buddhist temples.

clue: Dublin, Ireland 🇮🇪
fact: Ireland's capital grew from a Viking settlement founded around 841 on the River Liffey.

clue: Edinburgh, Scotland 🇬🇧
fact: Scotland's capital is dominated by a volcanic crag topped with a castle that's been fortified for nearly 900 years.

clue: Helsinki, Finland 🇫🇮
fact: Finland's capital sits on a peninsula and archipelago in the Baltic, and is one of the northernmost capitals in the EU.

clue: Santiago, Chile 🇨🇱
fact: Chile's capital sits in a valley ringed by the Andes, close enough that snow-capped peaks loom over the skyline.

clue: Casablanca, Morocco 🇲🇦
fact: Morocco's largest city is home to the Hassan II Mosque, whose minaret is one of the tallest religious structures in the world.

clue: Where do over a million wildebeest migrate across open grassland each year?
fact: This Tanzanian ecosystem hosts the largest terrestrial mammal migration on Earth, a circuit covering roughly 1,000 kilometers.

clue: Where did a young naturalist's finch observations help inspire the theory of evolution?
fact: Charles Darwin visited this volcanic archipelago in 1835, and its isolated wildlife shaped his thinking on natural selection.

clue: Where is a lake so salty that swimmers float effortlessly on its surface?
fact: At roughly 430 meters below sea level, its shore is the lowest point on dry land on Earth.

clue: Where does a building that has served as both a cathedral and a mosque stand?
fact: Completed in 537 AD as a Byzantine cathedral, it held the record for the world's largest interior space for nearly a thousand years.

clue: Where does the Moorish palace and fortress complex called the Alhambra stand?
fact: This Nasrid dynasty palace in Granada is famed for intricate tile and stucco work that inspired M.C. Escher's tessellation art.

clue: Where were thousands of life-sized clay soldiers buried to guard an emperor's tomb?
fact: Farmers digging a well in 1974 stumbled on this army of over 8,000 unique terracotta warriors near Xi'an, China.

clue: Where is the historic Swahili port city at the heart of the spice-trading Zanzibar archipelago?
fact: This Indian Ocean island's Stone Town was a hub of the 19th-century spice and slave trade under Omani Arab rule.

clue: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia 🇪🇹
fact: Ethiopia's capital sits at nearly 2,400 meters elevation, making it one of the highest capital cities in the world.

clue: Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia 🇲🇳
fact: The coldest national capital on Earth, it began as a mobile Buddhist monastic center before settling permanently in 1778.

clue: Quito, Ecuador 🇪🇨
fact: Ecuador's capital sits in an Andean valley almost exactly on the equator, at an elevation of nearly 2,850 meters.

clue: Tbilisi, Georgia 🇬🇪
fact: Georgia's capital grew around natural sulfur hot springs that still feed its old bathhouse district.

clue: Where does the world's largest salt flat turn into a giant mirror after rain?
fact: This Bolivian flat covers over 10,000 square kilometers and holds roughly half the world's known lithium reserves.

clue: Where were eleven churches carved downward out of solid volcanic rock?
fact: According to tradition, Ethiopia's King Lalibela ordered them built in the 12th century after a vision of Jerusalem.

clue: Where do hot air balloons drift over valleys of cone-shaped 'fairy chimney' rock formations?
fact: Early Christians carved entire underground cities and cave churches into this soft volcanic rock in central Turkey.

clue: Where do a chain of turquoise lakes cascade over travertine waterfalls?
fact: This Croatian national park's 16 terraced lakes are colored by minerals and shift shade with the light and season.

clue: Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan 🇰🇬
fact: Founded as a Russian fortress in 1825, Kyrgyzstan's capital sits in a valley ringed by the snow-capped Tian Shan mountains.

clue: Vientiane, Laos 🇱🇦
fact: Laos's capital on the Mekong River is one of the least densely populated capital cities in Asia.

clue: Asmara, Eritrea 🇪🇷
fact: Eritrea's capital is a UNESCO-listed showcase of 1930s Italian Art Deco architecture, nicknamed 'Piccola Roma.'

clue: Suva, Fiji 🇫🇯
fact: Fiji's capital sits on a peninsula on the island of Viti Levu and is one of the wettest capitals on Earth.

clue: Where did a legendary trans-Saharan trading city become synonymous with remoteness?
fact: This Malian city flourished in the 14th century as a center of gold, salt, and Islamic scholarship, home to thousands of ancient manuscripts.

clue: Where do alien-looking dragon's blood trees grow on an isolated island?
fact: Isolated for millions of years in the Arabian Sea, this Yemeni island has a third of its plant species found nowhere else on Earth.

clue: Where do white mineral terraces cascade down a hillside like frozen waterfalls?
fact: Calcium-rich hot springs have built up these white travertine terraces in Turkey over thousands of years.

clue: Where is one of the hottest and lowest places on Earth, dotted with sulfur springs and lava lakes?
fact: This Ethiopian desert basin sits over 100 meters below sea level and includes Erta Ale, one of the few volcanoes with a permanent lava lake.

clue: Thimphu, Bhutan 🇧🇹
fact: Bhutan's capital has no traffic lights, directed instead by white-gloved officers, and is one of the few capitals without them.

clue: Nuuk, Greenland 🇬🇱
fact: Greenland's capital is one of the smallest capital cities by population anywhere, founded as a trading post in 1728.

clue: Palikir, Micronesia 🇫🇲
fact: This capital of the Federated States of Micronesia sits on Pohnpei island and is home to only a few thousand people.

clue: Vaduz, Liechtenstein 🇱🇮
fact: The capital of this tiny Alpine microstate is overlooked by a castle still owned by the ruling prince's family.

clue: Pyongyang, North Korea 🇰🇵
fact: North Korea's capital was almost entirely rebuilt after the Korean War, with wide boulevards designed around monumental architecture.

clue: Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso 🇧🇫
fact: Burkina Faso's capital takes its name from two Mossi kingdoms whose rulers merged centuries ago.

clue: Where does a red-sand desert of towering sandstone cliffs evoke a landscape from Mars?
fact: Nicknamed the 'Valley of the Moon,' this desert has stood in for Mars in several Hollywood films.

clue: Where does a giant bullseye-shaped rock formation visible from space sit in the Sahara?
fact: Nicknamed the 'Eye of the Sahara,' this Mauritanian formation is roughly 40 kilometers wide and was long mistaken for a meteorite impact.

clue: Yaren, Nauru 🇳🇷
fact: This is the de facto capital of Nauru, the world's third-smallest country, an island once stripped bare by phosphate mining.

clue: Funafuti, Tuvalu 🇹🇻
fact: Tuvalu's capital atoll averages only about 2 meters above sea level, making it one of the first places threatened by rising seas.

clue: Ngerulmud, Palau 🇵🇼
fact: One of the least populated national capitals on Earth, it was purpose-built in the 2000s and has only a few hundred residents.

clue: Avarua, Cook Islands 🇨🇰
fact: This capital of a self-governing Pacific nation in free association with New Zealand sits on the island of Rarotonga.

clue: Longyearbyen, Svalbard 🇳🇴
fact: This Arctic settlement is the world's northernmost town of real size, and local rules require carrying a rifle outside town against polar bears.

clue: Where is the most remote inhabited island in the world?
fact: This South Atlantic island's main settlement, Edinburgh of the Seven Seas, lies about 2,400 kilometers from the nearest other inhabited land.

clue: Where is the point in the ocean farthest from any land?
fact: Named after Jules Verne's submarine captain, this spot in the South Pacific is so remote that astronauts in orbit are sometimes the closest humans to it.

clue: Where is the deepest known point in all of Earth's oceans?
fact: At nearly 11,000 meters down in the Mariana Trench, the pressure here is over 1,000 times that at the ocean's surface.

clue: Where is the largest research station on the coldest continent?
fact: This US Antarctic base sits on volcanic rock and can swell to over 1,000 people in the austral summer.

clue: Where was the coldest temperature ever recorded on Earth's surface?
fact: This Russian station recorded -89.2°C in 1983 and sits atop nearly 4 kilometers of Antarctic ice covering a hidden freshwater lake.

clue: Where did the mutineers of HMS Bounty hide from the Royal Navy?
fact: This tiny Pacific island's roughly 40 residents are mostly descended from the 1789 Bounty mutineers and their Tahitian companions.

clue: Where is the remote settlement of Ittoqqortoormiit, beside the world’s largest fjord system?
fact: One of the most isolated settlements in the Northern Hemisphere, it's reachable only by boat in summer or plane year-round, with no roads connecting it to anywhere.

clue: Where is the northernmost permanently inhabited place on Earth?
fact: This Canadian Forces station sits just 817 kilometers from the North Pole, closer to Russia's coast than to most of Canada.

clue: Where is the highest permanent human settlement on Earth?
fact: This Peruvian gold-mining town sits above 5,100 meters in the Andes, where the air holds about half the oxygen found at sea level.

clue: Where is Oymyakon, one of the coldest permanently inhabited places on Earth?
fact: Regularly cited as the coldest permanently inhabited place on Earth, it recorded a low of -67.7°C, and locals keep car engines running all day in winter.

clue: Where is the most remote island on the planet, uninhabited and almost entirely covered by a glacier?
fact: This Norwegian volcanic island in the South Atlantic lies over 1,600 kilometers from the nearest land, Antarctica.

fact: South Africa's largest city, known as the City of Gold, grew rapidly after gold was discovered on the Witwatersrand in 1886.

clue: Durban, South Africa 🇿🇦
fact: One of South Africa's major port cities, known for its African, Indian and colonial influences.

clue: Pretoria, South Africa 🇿🇦
fact: South Africa's administrative capital, known for its jacaranda-lined streets.

clue: Alexandria, Egypt 🇪🇬

clue: Luxor, Egypt 🇪🇬
fact: Built on the site of ancient Thebes, Luxor is home to some of Egypt's most spectacular archaeological sites.

clue: Aswan, Egypt 🇪🇬
fact: An important ancient trading city on the Nile, known for its granite quarries and the Aswan High Dam.

clue: Tunis, Tunisia 🇹🇳

clue: Algiers, Algeria 🇩🇿
fact: Algeria's capital, known as 'Algiers the White', is built on a hill overlooking the Mediterranean.

clue: Rabat, Morocco 🇲🇦
fact: Morocco's capital, a coastal city with a well-preserved historic medina and Kasbah of the Udayas.

clue: Fez, Morocco 🇲🇦
fact: One of Morocco's imperial cities, home to one of the world's oldest continuously operating universities, Al Quaraouiyine.

clue: Dakar, Senegal 🇸🇳

clue: Accra, Ghana 🇬🇭
fact: Ghana's capital and largest city, a major port on the Gulf of Guinea.

clue: Kinshasa, DR Congo 🇨🇩
fact: The capital of the Democratic Republic of Congo and Africa's most populous francophone city.

clue: Kigali, Rwanda 🇷🇼
fact: Rwanda's capital, known for its cleanliness and well-organized urban layout.

clue: Kampala, Uganda 🇺🇬
fact: Uganda's capital, built on several hills and near Lake Victoria.

clue: Dar es Salaam, Tanzania 🇹🇿
fact: Tanzania's largest city and former capital, an important commercial port on the Indian Ocean.

clue: Antananarivo, Madagascar 🇲🇬
fact: Madagascar's capital, built on hills and known for its colorful historic buildings.

clue: Maputo, Mozambique 🇲🇿
fact: Mozambique's capital, known for its Portuguese colonial architecture and vibrant culture.

clue: Harare, Zimbabwe 🇿🇼
fact: Zimbabwe's capital, known for its wide streets lined with jacaranda trees.

clue: Lusaka, Zambia 🇿🇲
fact: Zambia's capital, located in the country's central plateau region.

clue: Luanda, Angola 🇦🇴
fact: Angola's capital and one of Africa's most expensive cities, located on the Atlantic coast.

clue: Bamako, Mali 🇲🇱

clue: Tripoli, Libya 🇱🇾

clue: Kumasi, Ghana 🇬🇭
fact: The capital of the Ashanti Region, known for its rich cultural heritage and vibrant markets.

clue: Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire 🇨🇮
fact: Côte d'Ivoire's economic capital, known for its modern skyscrapers and lagoon system.

clue: Where is the ancient walled city of Kano, long a center of trans-Saharan trade?

clue: Mombasa, Kenya 🇰🇪
fact: Kenya's oldest and second-largest city, an important port on the Indian Ocean.

clue: Where is Arusha, the safari gateway beneath Mount Meru?

clue: Where is the Cape of Good Hope?

fact: An archaeological site in Tanzania where some of the earliest hominid fossils have been found.

clue: Where is Thabana Ntlenyana?

clue: Where are the Tsingy de Bemaraha?

clue: Where are the Kilwa Kisiwani Ruins?

clue: Where is Fort Jesus in Mombasa?

clue: Where is the Ngorongoro Crater rim lookout?
fact: The world's largest inactive, intact volcanic caldera, located in Tanzania.

clue: Where are the Three Rondavels in Blyde River Canyon?
fact: Iconic rock formations in one of the largest canyons on Earth, located in Mpumalanga.

clue: Where is Fasil Ghebbi?

clue: Where is Spitzkoppe?

clue: Where is the Temple of Amun at Naqa?

clue: Where are the Djemila Ruins?

fact: A 14th-century Islamic college in Marrakech, renowned for its intricate tilework and carvings.

clue: Where is the Koutoubia Mosque?
fact: Marrakech's most famous landmark, built in the 12th century with a 69-meter minaret.

clue: Where are the Sabratha Ruins?
fact: Ancient Roman city on Libya's Mediterranean coast, known for its stunning theatre.

clue: Where is Emi Koussi?
fact: Chad's highest mountain and the highest point in the Sahara Desert, a massive shield volcano.

clue: Where is Pico do Fogo?
fact: Cape Verde's highest peak and an active stratovolcano on Fogo Island.

clue: Where is Mount Karthala?
fact: An active shield volcano and the highest point in the Comoros archipelago.

clue: Where is Fort São Sebastião on Ilha de Moçambique?
fact: A 16th-century Portuguese fort on the Island of Mozambique, a UNESCO World Heritage site.

clue: Where is the Valley of the Queens?
fact: A burial site for queens and royal children of the 19th and 20th dynasties near Luxor.

clue: Manila, Philippines 🇵🇾d
fact: Intramuros, the walled Spanish city built around the Pasig River, was so badly destroyed in 1945 that only one of its original gates, San Luis, still stands.

clue: Osaka, Japan 🇯🇵
fact: Japan's 'kitchen' is built on eighteen artificial islands and stands where Naniwa stood, the first imperial capital ever recorded by name in writing.

clue: Tehran, Iran 🇮🇷
fact: The capital sinks by as much as 3 cm a year as the alluvial fan it was built on compacts, cracking metro tunnels and pulling old aqueducts out of line.

clue: Riyadh, Saudi Arabia 🇸🇦
fact: Saudi Arabia's royal palaces only appeared after 1970, when King Faisal abandoned the mudbrick walled oasis town and drew a modern capital along the Wadi Hanifa.

clue: Dhaka, Bangladesh 🇧🇩
fact: Millions still cross the Buriganga to reach work by launch, and the city employs well over a million garment workers sewing clothes exported under other countries' labels.

clue: Taipei, Taiwan 🇹🇼
fact: The capital's skyscraper Taipei 101 is planted with roughly 660,000 native Taiwanese plants, more greenery than any other tower in the world.

clue: Hanoi, Vietnam 🇷🇳
fact: Vietnam's capital marked its 1,000th anniversary in 2010, and its Old Quarter still folds away 27 km of alleyways narrow enough for two motorbikes to pass.

clue: Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia 🇲🇾
fact: Its Petronas Towers held the record for world's tallest buildings from 1998 to 2004, and the city's name simply means the muddy confluence where two rivers meet.

clue: Mecca, Saudi Arabia 🇸🇦
fact: More than 1.8 million pilgrims circle the Kaaba counter-clockwise five times each Hajj season, inside the largest mosque complex in the world.

clue: Hiroshima, Japan 🇯🇵
fact: The city's Peace Memorial Park sits on the hypocenter of the 1945 atomic bombing, which killed an estimated 140,000 people by the end of that year.

clue: Xi'an, China 🇨🇳
fact: Xi'an was the capital of thirteen dynasties and the eastern terminus of the Silk Road, whose worn paving stones still surface in the city.

clue: Hangzhou, China 🇨🇳
fact: The famous West Lake was named for sitting west of the city, was largely dug and embanked by hand, and has been rebuilt so often no original shoreline survives.

clue: Kolkata, India 🇮🇳
fact: Kolkata is the only Indian city where trams still run along main streets, and its humid heat plus grand colonial houses earned it the nickname 'City of Palaces'.

clue: Varanasi, India 🇮🇳
fact: More than 80 ghats step down to the Ganges here, and the Manikarnika cremation ground is so ancient that Hindu myth says Shiva himself chose it for burning.

clue: Jaipur, India 🇮🇳
fact: Laid out in 1727, Jaipur was India's first planned city, built in a strict nine-square grid of pink sandstone blocks.

clue: Lahore, Pakistan 🇵🇰
fact: The Badshahi Mosque and Lahore Fort were built to rival the Ottoman mosques of Istanbul, and the fort's Sheesh Mahal mirrors candle flames through thousands of cut-glass tiles.

clue: Karachi, Pakistan 🇵🇰
fact: Karachi went from a small fishing village to Pakistan's largest city inside a single century, and its colonial Mohatta Palace now houses the national gallery.

clue: Damascus, Syria 🇸🇦🇸
fact: Damascus is often called the oldest continuously inhabited city in the world, with layers of settlement stacked directly beneath its modern streets.

clue: Beirut, Lebanon 🇱🇧
fact: The shell-shattered downtown was rebuilt in the 1990s after fifteen years of civil war, and some bullet-scarred facades were deliberately preserved as memorials.

clue: Doha, Qatar 🇶🇦
fact: The Museum of Islamic Art here was designed entirely by I. M. Pei and reopened in 2023 after seven years of restoration, on its own artificial island.

clue: Baghdad, Iraq 🇮🇵
fact: Founded in 762 by the Abbasids, the city ran the world's first paper mill, turning Chinese papermaking into the writing medium of the Islamic world.

clue: Kathmandu, Nepal 🇳🇵
fact: The Kumari Ghar still houses the living goddess Kumari, who in modern times has never once left the palace during her lifetime.

clue: Yangon, Myanmar 🇲🇲
fact: Myanmar's largest city grew up around Shwedagon Pagoda, whose 99 m stupa has been re-plated with pilgrims' donated gold leaf so often it gleams from the air.

clue: Sapporo, Japan 🇯🇵
fact: Every February the city hosts the Snow Festival, where crews race to set snow-sculpture records, and it hosted the 1972 Winter Olympics.

clue: Busan, South Korea 🇰🇷
fact: Gamcheon Culture Village was built as a hillside refuge for Korean War refugees and is now stacked with pastel houses linked by hundreds of alley stairways.

clue: Amritsar, India 🇮🇳
fact: The Golden Temple's kitchen serves free meals to up to 100,000 people a day, and the city holds India's first Sikh gurdwara beside a well where Guru Nanak is said to have bathed.

clue: Where is Udaipur, the “City of Lakes” known for its white palace on Lake Pichola?
fact: The white City Palace, still home to the Mewar royal family after four centuries, overlooks Lake Pichola, an artificial island made by damming a valley in the 14th century.

clue: Where is Kanyakumari, where three seas meet at the southern tip of a subcontinent?
fact: At India's southern tip, where the Arabian Sea, the Bay of Bengal and the Indian Ocean meet, a Vivekananda Rock Memorial honors the spot where the sage is said to have meditated in 1892.

clue: Medina, Saudi Arabia 🇸🇦
fact: The Prophet's Mosque here was the first mosque built under Muslim rule in Arabia, and its courtyards were expanded so often that they now nest inside one another.

clue: Isfahan, Iran 🇮🇷
fact: Its Imam Square once covered more ground than Rome's Piazza San Marco, and the Safavid capital's blue-tiled mausoleums still run with water from fountains that worked for centuries.

clue: Tashkent, Uzbekistan 🇺🇫
fact: The 1966 earthquake flattened most of this Central Asian city's historic core, which planners then rebuilt from scratch in wide Soviet-era boulevards.

clue: Almaty, Kazakhstan 🇰🇱
fact: Kazakhstan's former capital still supplies most of the world's apple crop, and Medeu, just above the city, holds Olympic ice at 1,691 m, the highest in the world.

clue: Baku, Azerbaijan 🇦🇬
fact: Baku's Old City is ringed by the thickest surviving fortress walls in Iran and contains the Qiz Qala Maiden Tower, while glass skyscrapers rise directly behind it.

clue: Amman, Jordan 🇯🇴
fact: Amman's downtown sits seven levels below today's street, where a Roman theatre cut for 6,000 spectators was carved straight into the hillside above it.

clue: Phnom Penh, Cambodia 🇰🇬
fact: The Royal Palace stands where a bridge was thrown across the Mekong in the 1440s by pre-Angkorian kings, and the Killing Fields nearby hold the graves of over 17,000 people killed from 1975 to 1979.

clue: Malé, Maldives 🇲🇮
fact: The world's most densely populated capital is squeezed onto a coral strip under 2 km long, and every seawall it builds pushes the atoll's edge further into the Indian Ocean.

clue: George Town, Malaysia 🇲🇾
fact: Penang's clan jetties have stood on stilts above the water for more than two centuries, and the UNESCO zone of 18th-century timber shophouses is one of Southeast Asia's largest.

clue: Dili, Timor-Leste 🇱🇹
fact: Portuguese tile roofs, pastel houses and Catholic plazas line this crescent bay, and a dozen mass graves found after 1998 hold more than 10,000 bodies.

clue: Vladivostok, Russia 🇷🇺
fact: A Soviet decree kept foreigners out until 1992, and the city's terminus anchors the 9,289 km Trans-Siberian Railway, the longest in the world.

clue: Where is the lakeside city of Van, overlooked by an ancient citadel?
fact: Lake Ercek sits nearly 1,190 m above sea level beside the city, and the Urartian citadel of Toprakkale still stands on a rock just offshore.

clue: Kandahar, Afghanistan 🇦🇫
fact: Founded by Alexander's veterans as a market town, Kandahar's walls still carry two talisman-studded gate bosses driven into them after Nadir Shah's 1737 sack.

clue: Where is Leh, the high-altitude former caravan hub in the Indus Valley?
fact: This Ladakh capital stands at 3,500 m on a flood plain between bare mountains, and the road in from Srinagar is open only from late May to October.

clue: Where is Luang Prabang, the former royal capital at the meeting of the Mekong and Nam Khan rivers?
fact: Gold-roofed temples and the former royal palace sit on a peninsula where the Mekong and Nam Khan rivers meet, and the town's main street has been kept free of cars.

clue: Where is Shigatse, home to Tashilhunpo Monastery and the Panchen Lamas?
fact: Shigatse's Tashilhunpo Monastery, seat of the Panchen Lamas, holds China's largest gilded Buddha statue and stands across the Tsangpo River from the old town.

clue: Where does a palace of twenty-four emperors stand behind a wide moat in China's capital?
fact: Ming and Qing emperors lived inside these walls from 1420 to 1924, and the surviving complex still covers 72 hectares across some 980 buildings.

clue: Where does a six-minaret mosque glow blue over Istanbul's old city?
fact: Built 1609-1616 for Sultan Ahmed I, its interior is lined with more than 20,000 İznik tiles, and it was designed to rival Hagia Sophia just across the square.

clue: Where did Ottoman sultans rule for four centuries behind walls above the Bosphorus?
fact: From these ramparts the Janissaries' bodies were flung onto the city below, and the palace harem keeps relics said to have belonged to the Prophet Muhammad.

clue: Where does the main royal palace of the Joseon dynasty change guards twice a day in full period costume?
fact: Rebuilt in 1865 after the first palace burned down, its changing of the guard ceremony still recreates the 15th-century ritual of the Joseon kings.

clue: Where does the world's highest mountain pierce the sky?
fact: At 8,849 m Everest is the Nepal-China border peak, and because of the border dispute Nepal's own maps show it as 8,586 m, which makes the country's highest peak the world's 14th.

clue: Where does the largest Buddhist temple in the world climb a volcanic hill in Java?
fact: Built in the 8th-9th century, it wraps 2,672 relief panels around nine stacked platforms, and work stopped in 1006 when the volcano erupted and buried the site.

clue: Where does a 71 m Buddha carved from a cliff watch three rivers meet?
fact: Cut between 1001 and 1153, the figure is so large that a Song emperor once considered damming the river to drown it, and it still holds its own stone umbrella against the weather.

clue: Where do 1,600 limestone towers rise sheer out of the sea?
fact: Marine paleontologists once proposed pouring fossil fuel into these caves to date the world's oldest tropical limestone, and no one has found a better explanation for the karsts' odd chemistry.

clue: Where does a hilltop palace above Jaipur mirror 2,000 pieces of cut glass?
fact: Amber Fort was built with one of the world's earliest formal gardens, laid out in the same nine-square pattern as the planned city that grew below it.

clue: Where do thousands of vermilion torii gates tunnel up a hillside in Kyoto?
fact: Every gate is a donation from a Japanese company, which is why the tunnels never end, and the shrines at the summit are said to grant prosperity in trading.

clue: Where do three grand madrasas frame the great public square of Samarkand?
fact: The square's buildings date from the 1400s to the 1600s, and beside it stood Ulugh Beg's observatory, which measured the length of the year to within a second.

clue: Where do 500 painted caves hold 45 km of Buddhist murals in a desert cliff?
fact: The caves were sealed for a thousand years when sand blew into the library cave, which preserved tens of thousands of scroll paintings dry.

clue: Where do the Dalai Lamas' thirteen-storey winter palace rise above Lhasa at 3,700 m?
fact: The palace was fired in 1959 and rebuilt from the walls that survived, while thousands of monks and nuns had already been expelled from the city.

clue: Where do forested sandstone pillars inspired the floating mountains of a blockbuster?
fact: More than 3,000 quartz pillars rise here on narrow pillars of their own, and a glass bridge opened across the deepest canyon between two of them in 2016.

clue: Where is the highest mountain in Southeast Asia?
fact: At 4,095 m Kinabalu's bare granite summit sits on a still-uplifting fault block, and glaciers that once covered it have been gone since the last ice age.

clue: Where is a fifth-century royal citadel carved into a 200 m rock, guarded by a monumental lion gateway?
fact: The Lion Rock's terraces hold a fresco of a 'cloud woman' nearly identical to one painted at an Indian temple, and the two designs are thought to share a single source.

clue: Where did over 2,000 Buddhist temples once stand on a single plain?
fact: The temples of Bagan were built between 1001 and 1287 on money raised by 10,000 donor inscriptions carved into the sandalwood slabs now kept in museums.

clue: Where has a desert gas fire been burning for half a century?
fact: Soviet geologists lit this natural gas well alight in 1971 expecting it to burn out in weeks; the crater is a 70 m pit of flame that has never gone out.

clue: Where does a Gobi ridge of red cliffs glow like fire at sunset?
fact: The orange sandstone of Bayanzag burned red at dusk long before it was named, and dinosaur skeletons excavated in the 1920s made the site famous for fossils as well.

clue: Where is the second-longest alpine lake in the world, which never freezes?
fact: At 6,248 m in the Kyrgyz Tien Shan, it holds more water by volume than Lake Baikal and was drained by a pre-Catalan-era king who was afraid of the water spirits.

clue: Where were monumental T-shaped stone pillars carved more than 11,000 years ago?
fact: Hunter-gatherers, not farmers, raised this hilltop of enclosures around 9600 BC, which upset the idea that settled agriculture had to come first, and the site was deliberately buried by hand.

clue: Where is a bricked and bitumen-sealed Great Bath from a city that vanished 4,500 years ago?
fact: The Indus metropolis on this mound was abandoned with no sign of warfare, and its drains were laid so carefully that a thousand years of traffic found no need for repairs.

clue: Where does a stone relief of 23 subject nations still watch an empty Persian terrace?
fact: This ceremonial capital of the Achaemenid empire was burned by Alexander in 330 BC, yet its gate, treasury columns and audience-hall stairs survive almost intact.

clue: Where did 10,000 monks study for centuries and coin the decimal zero?
fact: This monastery complex in Bihar ran for 700 years, and Chinese pilgrims who studied here carried its ideas home long before the Arabic al-khwarizmi made 'zero' a term Europe would adopt.

clue: Where did Akbar build a red-sandstone capital and abandon it after fourteen years?
fact: The Mughal emperor left this ghost city when the water ran out, and its Buland Darwaza triumphal gate is still the tallest gateway in the world.

clue: Where is a single stone slab inscribed with 1,400 lines of writing?
fact: Sri Lanka's second ancient capital has the Gal Potha, an 8 m stone 'book' that was struck by lightning and toppled in the 1600s, and its elephants still step out of their own shadows.

clue: Where did the opening shots of the Second Sino-Japanese War get fired in August 1937?
fact: A patrol of Japanese troops was refused entry to this Beijing bridge and a firefight began, and the Chinese still keep the old guardhouse as a memorial to the dead.

clue: Where is the world's largest cave passage, with its own jungle, river and clouds inside?
fact: The largest known cave passage system on Earth lay unexplored until 1991, when a climber squeezed through the entrance hole that a sinkhole in Laos had opened into its roof.

clue: Where was the capital of the Mongol Empire, built with bricks from its own temples?
fact: On the Orkhon River the city of Karakorum was raised from Buddhist sculptures and building material taken from Buddhist monuments, then abandoned after one summer of use.

clue: Where is an Indus city with a signboard older than Sumerian writing?
fact: Dholavira's excavators found a stone signboard of painted jars, a stone water-harvesting ring and a fortification that held for centuries, all on an island in Gujarat's Gulf of Kachchh.

clue: Where did a Gobi cliff yield a tyrannosaur egg nest of 22 intact eggs?
fact: The red rocks of this 'Flaming Wall' have given up dozens of dinosaur fossils since the 1920s, and the site is now closed to everyone but scientists for fear of theft.

clue: Where does the Pamir Highway top out, between Tajikistan and Kyrgyzstan?
fact: At 4,655 m this is the highest point on the road from Kashgar to Dushanbe, and in winter the pass is closed entirely as ice cliffs hang over the tarmac.

clue: Where is the walled former capital of Mustang, a kingdom in the Himalayas near Tibet?
fact: This plateau town in Mustang is the old capital of the walled Himalayan kingdom of Lo, whose king married a Chinese princess in 1951 after generations of border hostility.

clue: Where is the world's oldest known port, with a dockyard built of stamped bricks?
fact: This Indus town on Gujarat's coast was among the world's earliest planned cities, and its tidal dockyard is built from bricks stamped with the year they were fired.

clue: Where is a glacial lake so high that legends say the goddess Nanda Devi appeared in it?
fact: In Ladakh's upper Bhagirathi valley the lake sits in a basin around 5,050 m, where pilgrims once walked up to see the reflection of the goddess and the surrounding peaks.

clue: Where does a chain of sandbars, called Rama Setu in Hindu tradition, connect two countries?
fact: The 80 km chain of shoals between India and Sri Lanka is described as a natural bridge in the Ramayana, but sonar surveys found no channel deep enough for stone piers.

clue: Madrid, Spain 🇪🇸
fact: Madrid's Puerta del Sol is the literal zero point of Spain's whole road and rail network, so every kilometre in the country is measured outward from it.

clue: Florence, Italy 🇮🇹
fact: Florence's Arno flooded in 1552 and legend says shoemakers soaked their leather hides overnight to raise the river and drown the plague victims in its mud.

clue: Lisbon, Portugal 🇵🇹
fact: Lisbon is the westernmost capital of the European Union, so every sunset there is the last sunset of the EU.

clue: Budapest, Hungary 🇭🇺
fact: Budapest sits on more than a hundred thermal springs, and the Romans bathed in them at Aquincum nearly two thousand years ago.

clue: Warsaw, Poland 🇵🇱
fact: After 1944 the Nazis blew up about 85% of Warsaw and left it standing in ruins, so almost everything you see today was rebuilt brick by brick.

clue: Stockholm, Sweden 🇸🇪
fact: Stockholm is spread across fourteen islands stitched together by around thirty bridges, which is why it is called the Venice of the North.

clue: Kyiv, Ukraine 🇺🇦
fact: Kyiv's Monastery of the Caves preserves the world's first ever recorded jump: in 1086 a monk leapt from a church tower and survived to write it down.

clue: Saint Petersburg, Russia 🇷🇺
fact: Saint Petersburg was built on a swamp of more than a hundred islands, with millions of oak logs driven into the marsh to shore up its foundations.

clue: Munich, Germany 🇩🇪
fact: Munich's oldest beer rules date to 1487, and Hofbrauhaus has been brewing to them without interruption since 1589.

clue: Naples, Italy 🇮🇹
fact: Naples holds the world's oldest pizzeria still cooking in its original wood oven, Antica Pizzeria Port'Alba, fired since 1538.

clue: Seville, Spain 🇪🇸
fact: Seville's Giralda tower began life as the minaret of the Almohad mosque, and its bell was rung as a city alarm from the twelfth century on.

clue: Porto, Portugal 🇵🇹
fact: Port wine takes its name from Porto but was never made there; it is blended and aged in the lodges of Vila Nova de Gaia across the Douro.

clue: Brussels, Belgium 🇧🇪
fact: Brussels gave the world the Brussels sprout, and for centuries English speakers called the vegetable by the city's name before the French did.

clue: Zurich, Switzerland 🇨🇭
fact: Zurich ranks as the most expensive city on earth by cost of living, and its Bahnhofstrasse was lit by electric lamps before almost any other street in Europe.

clue: Hamburg, Germany 🇩🇪
fact: Hamburg's port, working without interruption since 1189, is Germany's largest and among Europe's busiest, and its Speicherstadt still warehouses coffee and spices.

clue: Krakow, Poland 🇵🇱
fact: Krakow's Rynek Underground museum sets a glass floor over excavated medieval market stalls in the middle of what is Europe's largest medieval town square.

clue: Copenhagen, Denmark 🇩🇰
fact: Copenhagen's sperm bank, started in 1954 by a handful of students, now holds more than half a million jars of donated donor sperm.

clue: Oslo, Norway 🇳🇴
fact: Oslo city hall is where every Nobel Peace Prize laureate signs the visitors' book, the one ceremony the Nobel prizes still hold outside Sweden.

clue: Manchester, England, United Kingdom 🇬🇧
fact: Britain's first inter-city passenger train arrived at Manchester's Hunts Bank in 1830, and Ancoats was the world's first great factory district.

clue: Oxford, England, United Kingdom 🇬🇧
fact: Oxford's Ashmolean, opened in 1683, is Britain's first public museum, and the university's teaching tradition predates the Aztec empire.

clue: Dubrovnik, Croatia 🇭🇷
fact: Dubrovnik declared itself a republic to rival Venice, and its 1,940-metre circuit of walls is among the thickest stone fortifications ever built.

clue: Zagreb, Croatia 🇭🇷
fact: Zagreb's Upper Town clings to a volcanic hill, and its Gri cannon has fired one blank charge every New Year's Eve since 1815 to scare off bad spirits.

clue: Glasgow, Scotland, United Kingdom 🇬🇧
fact: Glasgow shipped the cigars of the British Empire from the Clyde, earning the titles Cigarette City and Second City of the Empire.

clue: Liverpool, England, United Kingdom 🇬🇧
fact: Liverpool's docks handled more world trade than any other port for most of the nineteenth century, and its band scene gave the world four of the Beatles.

clue: Belgrade, Serbia 🇷🇸
fact: Belgrade stands where the Sava meets the Danube and has been besieged, sacked and burnt so often over the centuries that it holds the European record.

clue: Sofia, Bulgaria 🇧🇬
fact: Sofia stands on a cluster of mineral springs, and the Romans of Serdica heated their city and their baths with water drawn from the same springs.

clue: Bucharest, Romania 🇷🇴
fact: Bucharest's Palace of the Parliament, at 3,700 tonnes the heaviest building ever constructed, towers over an old town it would flatten in an afternoon.

clue: Tallinn, Estonia 🇪🇪
fact: Tallinn's Old Town is a walled Hanseatic city left so intact that its town hall square doubles as an ice rink every winter.

clue: Bruges, Belgium 🇧🇪
fact: Bruges' canals were dug deep enough for merchant ships to unload at the market squares themselves, making it the busiest trading port in northern Europe.

clue: Dresden, Germany 🇩🇪
fact: Dresden's Frauenkirche was taken apart stone by stone after the 1945 bombing and rebuilt to within millimetres of its original height.

clue: Salzburg, Austria 🇦🇹
fact: Salzburg's squares, lanes and hilltop fortress were the filming locations for The Sound of Music in 1965, and the trails that follow them now fill the old town.

clue: Bergen, Norway 🇳🇴
fact: Bergen's wooden Bryggen wharf has been burnt down and rebuilt no fewer than seven times since the first fire in 1702.

clue: Turin, Italy 🇮🇹
fact: Turin gave the world the Fiat 500, launched here as the tiny Topolino in 1957, and its automobile museum grew from the car collection of the first House of Savoy.

clue: Bilbao, Spain 🇪🇸
fact: Frank Gehry's Guggenheim Bilbao opened in 1997 and put the industrial Basque city on the world's tourist map within a decade.

clue: Ghent, Belgium 🇧🇪
fact: Ghent's Graslei and Korenlei quays still front the guild houses of the medieval wool merchants who made it one of Europe's richest cities.

clue: Where does the Hall of Mirrors gleam in the French palace that Louis XIV used to dominate Europe from?
fact: Versailles' Hall of Mirrors has 357 mirrors, and the Seine's water was pumped 13 kilometres by the Machine de Marly so the fountains could run every day.

clue: Where does the ancient Roman rotunda with a single oculus open onto the sky?
fact: The Panthe's oculus is one 43-metre hole cut in the dome and the only light the interior gets, so rain falls straight onto the marble floor.

clue: Where does the largest church in the world stand under the tallest dome in Rome?
fact: St Peter's dome rises 136.6 metres, second only to Florence's Duomo, and it took four popes and nearly three centuries to finish.

clue: Where does a landmark Gothic cathedral raise twin spires above the Rhine?
fact: Cologne Cathedral took 632 years to finish, and during the Second World War Allied bombs failed to bring down its twin spires.

clue: Where does the gateway with a four-horse chariot on top mark the start of Berlin's main avenue?
fact: Napoleon marched through the Brandenburg Gate into Berlin in 1806, and the Quadriga on top did not come home until 1958.

clue: Where does a stone fortress still keep its ravens, crown jewels and prison cells?
fact: The Tower of London was a royal palace for four centuries before becoming a prison and armoury, and its ravens are the last of a flock kept since the Wild Men.

clue: Where does the onion-domed cathedral with nine chapels and one bell tower stand on Red Square?
fact: St Basil's was named after a holy fool and not after Basil the Great, and it was built in 1561 to mark the capture of Kazan and Astrakhan.

clue: Where does the Parthenon still guard the marble hill above the ancient city?
fact: The Parthenon's corner columns are 2.4% thicker than the middle ones and lean inward, an optical correction that has kept them looking upright for 2,400 years.

clue: Where does the still-unfinished basilica of spires like honeycombs stand?
fact: Gaudi's Sagrada Familia has been under construction since 1882, and his plaster model of it was photographed from a reconnaissance aeroplane in 1926.

clue: Where can you read the wartime diary of a teenage girl in the room where she wrote it?
fact: Anne Frank's diary survived because Fritz Frank and Gies Huber abandoned papers before they were deported in 1942, and it was not published until 1947.

clue: Where does the neo-Gothic parliament with 691 statues face the Danube?
fact: Budapest's Parliament was sited deliberately across the river from Habsburg Buda so the Hungarian nation would stare back at the emperor's own palace.

clue: Where is the winter palace of the tsars turned museum holding millions of artworks?
fact: The Hermitage grew from the 317 paintings Catherine the Great bought in Dutch auctions, and for decades it had no public entrance at all.

clue: Where did a royal dynasty rule for five hundred years from a castle above the Vistula?
fact: Wawel Castle was the seat of Poland's kings for five centuries, and its dragon on the riverbank breathes real flame at visitors twice a day.

clue: Where does a 42-floor Stalin-era skyscraper, presented as a Soviet gift, dominate the skyline?
fact: The Palace of Culture was sent by Stalin to Poland in 1955 as a gift, its construction materials shipped in from 168 Soviet locations.

clue: Where do thirty baroque statues line the footbridge that linked Prague's two halves?
fact: Charles Bridge was the only crossing of the Vltava for five hundred years, and the crowning saint on it is Saint Wenceslas, the patron of Bohemia.

clue: Where does the 600-year-old clock show where the sun and the moon should be?
fact: Prague's astronomical clock has run since 1410, and its slow zodiac disc turns once for the 365 days of the year it keeps.

clue: Where do you climb the fortified circuit of stone walls around a walled Adriatic republic?
fact: UNESCO's inscription for Dubrovnik calls it a city built and defended over three centuries, and the walls enclose an old town barely 300 metres across.

clue: Where is the Carpathian castle whose name is linked for ever to Dracula?
fact: Bran Castle was raised in 1378 not as a royal seat but as a customs post and garrison guarding the trade route through the Carpathian passes.

clue: Where was the Roman town frozen in ash by a volcano in AD 79?
fact: Pompeii's plaster casts were poured into the cavities left by bodies decomposed in the ash, so figures still frozen mid-stride stand in their shops.

clue: Where does a hill fortress of 50 rooms watch over the rooftops of an Austrian music city?
fact: Hohensalzburg was finished in 1077 and never taken by assault; a legend says Salzburg's archbishop ordered all but one of its bells silenced as raving mad.

clue: Where do people still live in cave dwellings trodden out of a tuff cliff?
fact: Matera's cisterns under St Peter's Cave hold a cardinal's hat, a papal tiara and a belt preserved in a single drop of water that has not evaporated since the 1300s.

clue: Where do whitewashed cone-roofed trulli stand wall to wall like a village of beehives?

fact: Bogota's civic heart is named for independence leader Simon Bolivar. The square is framed by Colombia's principal institutions.

clue: Where is Plaza Independencia in Montevideo?
fact: This square separates Montevideo's old city from its modern center. A monument and mausoleum honor Jose Artigas.

clue: Where is Plaza Murillo in La Paz?
fact: Bolivia's executive and legislative buildings cluster around this historic plaza. It sits at roughly 3,650 meters above sea level.

clue: Where is the original salt hotel on Salar de Uyuni?
fact: The former Hotel de Sal Playa Blanca is built largely from blocks of salt. It now serves as a museum near the flats' Dakar monument.

clue: Where is the Base Torres viewpoint?
fact: This viewpoint faces the three sheer granite towers that give the Chilean park its name. Reaching it requires a demanding hike.

clue: Where are the Uros floating islands?
fact: The Uros build and maintain islands from layers of totora reeds on Lake Titicaca. Reed boats and homes use the same plant.

clue: Where is Botero Plaza in Medellin?
fact: The plaza displays 23 monumental bronze sculptures donated by Fernando Botero. The patterned Palace of Culture stands beside it.

clue: Where is the Amazon Theatre?
fact: Manaus built this lavish opera house during the rubber boom. Its dome is tiled in the colors of Brazil's flag.

clue: Where is the ALMA Observatory operations site?
fact: ALMA's radio antennas observe the cold universe from Chile's exceptionally dry high plateau. The array operates above 5,000 meters.

clue: Where is the Mitad del Mundo monument?
fact: This monument celebrates Ecuador's equatorial location. Modern measurements place the true equator a short distance away.

clue: Where is Valparaiso's Ascensor Artilleria?
fact: This funicular climbs between the port district and Paseo 21 de Mayo. It is one of the city's historic hillside elevators.

clue: Where is St. George's Cathedral in Georgetown?
fact: This Anglican cathedral is among the world's tallest wooden churches. Its Gothic spire rises above Guyana's capital.

clue: Where is Suriname's Presidential Palace?
fact: The white colonial-era palace faces Independence Square in Paramaribo's UNESCO-listed center. A palm garden lies behind it.

clue: Where is Cusco's Plaza de Armas?
fact: The square occupies part of the Inca ceremonial center once called Huacaypata. Spanish churches now rise over Inca foundations.

clue: Where is Maracana Stadium?
fact: Rio's famous stadium hosted decisive matches in two FIFA World Cups. It opened for the 1950 tournament.

clue: Where is the National Mint of Bolivia in Potosi?
fact: Colonial silver from Cerro Rico was coined in this vast mint. Its machinery and galleries document the city's extraordinary boom.

clue: Where is Porto Jofre, a gateway to the Pantanal?
fact: This small riverside outpost marks the southern end of the Transpantaneira. Boat trips from here are renowned for jaguar sightings.

clue: Where is the main viewpoint at Kaieteur Falls?
fact: The Potaro River drops in a single powerful plunge over Guyana's sandstone plateau. The falls are remote and usually reached by small aircraft.

clue: Where is the Cruz del Condor viewpoint?
fact: This ledge above Peru's Colca Canyon is celebrated for close views of soaring Andean condors. Thermal currents lift the birds past the rim.

clue: Where is the Lagoa Bonita viewpoint?
fact: Seasonal freshwater lagoons collect among immense white dunes near Barreirinhas. Lagoa Bonita is reached by a steep sand climb.

clue: Where is the historic center of Paraty?
fact: Paraty preserves cobbled streets and colonial buildings on Brazil's Costa Verde. High tides intentionally wash into parts of the old town.

clue: Where is the Kalasasaya temple at Tiwanaku?
fact: Tiwanaku was the ceremonial center of a major pre-Inca civilization. The famous Gateway of the Sun stands within the archaeological complex.

clue: Where is the Tschudi Palace at Chan Chan?
fact: Chan Chan was the capital of the Chimu kingdom and the largest adobe city in the Americas. Reliefs in its compounds evoke waves, fish, and seabirds.

clue: Where is the Bosque de las Estatuas at San Agustin?
fact: This Colombian archaeological park protects enigmatic stone figures made by a pre-Columbian culture. Many guarded monumental tombs.

clue: Where is Las Lajas Sanctuary?
fact: This neo-Gothic church bridges a deep gorge near Colombia's border with Ecuador. Its altar incorporates the cliff face.

clue: Where is the triple-border marker on Mount Roraima?
fact: A small monument marks the meeting of Venezuela, Guyana, and Brazil atop the tepui. The isolated summit supports unusual endemic plants.

clue: Where is Bariloche's Civic Centre?
fact: Bariloche's stone-and-timber civic complex faces Lake Nahuel Huapi. The city is Argentina's best-known gateway to the northern Patagonian lakes.

clue: Where is the Magellan monument in Punta Arenas?
fact: A bronze Ferdinand Magellan crowns the monument in the city's main square. Local tradition promises a return to Patagonia to those who touch its polished foot.

clue: Where is Ushuaia's End of the World sign?
fact: The waterfront sign celebrates Ushuaia's claim as the world's southernmost city. The Beagle Channel and Martial Mountains frame the setting.

clue: Where is Casa de la Libertad in Sucre?
fact: Bolivia's declaration of independence was signed in this former Jesuit building in 1825. It now serves as a national history museum.

clue: Where is Tiradentes Square in Ouro Preto?
fact: Baroque churches and steep colonial streets surround this former gold-rush capital. The square honors independence martyr Tiradentes.

clue: Where is the modernist National Congress complex designed by Oscar Niemeyer?
fact: Oscar Niemeyer designed the paired towers and opposing bowl-shaped chambers. The complex is a defining work of modernist Brasilia.

clue: Where is Marco Zero in Recife?
fact: This waterfront plaza is the official point from which road distances in Pernambuco are measured. A colorful compass mosaic fills its center.

clue: Where is Salvador's Largo do Pelourinho?
fact: Pastel-colored colonial buildings line this steep square in Salvador's historic center. It is a major center of Afro-Brazilian culture.

clue: Where is Cabo San Juan in Tayrona National Park?
fact: Twin Caribbean coves meet beneath a rocky lookout and hut. The beach is reached by trail or boat within Colombia's Tayrona park.

clue: Where is the Jose Rivas Refuge on Cotopaxi?
fact: This high-altitude refuge sits on the flank of one of the world's highest active volcanoes. Climbers use it as a base for summit attempts.

clue: Where is Cuenca's New Cathedral?
fact: Three enormous blue-tiled domes crown this Ecuadorian landmark. A design error meant its planned bell towers could not safely be completed.

clue: Where are the Chincana ruins on Isla del Sol?
fact: This Inca complex overlooks Lake Titicaca from the island's northern end. Its maze of stone rooms may have housed priests.

clue: Where is the Laguna de los Tres viewpoint?
fact: This glacial lake provides the classic close view of Mount Fitz Roy. The final approach is one of the steepest stretches of the trail.

clue: Where is Punta Norte on Peninsula Valdes?
fact: Sea lions and elephant seals gather along this remote Patagonian shore. Orcas sometimes use intentional stranding to hunt here.

clue: Where is the Lanzon temple at Chavin de Huantar?
fact: Underground galleries surround the carved Lanzon monolith at this ancient Andean ceremonial center. The site predates the Inca by well over a millennium.

clue: Where is the lighthouse in Colonia del Sacramento?
fact: The lighthouse rises through the ruins of a 17th-century convent. Its summit overlooks the Rio de la Plata and the old Portuguese quarter.

clue: Where is the ruined prison on Devil's Island?
fact: This tiny island off French Guiana formed part of the notorious penal colony known as the Salvation Islands. Alfred Dreyfus was imprisoned here.

clue: Where is the Guiana Space Centre's main launch zone?
fact: Europe launches rockets from near-equatorial French Guiana, where Earth's rotation provides an efficiency advantage. The spaceport began operating in 1968.

clue: Where is the Chuquicamata mine viewpoint?
fact: Chuquicamata is one of the world's largest open-pit copper mines. The neighboring company town was largely relocated because of environmental concerns.

clue: Where is the Hand of the Desert?
fact: Chilean sculptor Mario Irarrazabal's giant concrete hand rises from the Atacama beside the Pan-American Highway. It was unveiled in 1992.

clue: Where is the astronomical observatory in the Tatacoa badlands?
fact: Clear skies and low light pollution make this small Colombian observatory a popular stargazing site. Red and gray eroded formations surround it.

clue: Where is the main viewpoint over Quilotoa crater lake?
fact: A turquoise lake fills the caldera of this Ecuadorian volcano. Dissolved minerals help produce its changing color.

clue: Where is the Jesuit mission church of Concepcion?
fact: This richly decorated wooden church belongs to Bolivia's UNESCO-listed Jesuit Missions of Chiquitos. Its present reconstruction follows the original colonial design.

clue: Where is Santa Catalina Monastery?
fact: This vast walled convent in Arequipa resembles a small city of vivid lanes and cloisters. It was founded in 1579.

clue: Where is the main viewpoint at Laguna Colorada?
fact: Minerals and algae tint this shallow Bolivian lake red. Large flocks of flamingos feed in its high-altitude waters.

clue: Where is the lighthouse at Cabo Polonio?
fact: This lighthouse watches over a rocky Uruguayan cape reached across dunes by off-road vehicles. A large sea-lion colony occupies nearby islets.

clue: Where is Andre Kamperveen Stadium?
fact: Suriname's national stadium in Paramaribo is named for a footballer, broadcaster, and former national team captain. It hosts major domestic and international matches.

clue: Where is Fort Zeelandia in Paramaribo?
fact: This riverside fort records centuries of Dutch colonial history in Suriname. It now houses the Surinaams Museum.

clue: Where is Pedra Furada in Serra da Capivara?
fact: This natural rock arch stands amid one of South America's richest concentrations of prehistoric rock art. Nearby sites have fueled debate about the timing of human settlement.

clue: Where is Pucara de Tilcara?
fact: This reconstructed pre-Hispanic hilltop settlement overlooks Argentina's Quebrada de Humahuaca. Its position controlled movement through the valley.

clue: Where is Saint-Sauveur Cathedral in Cayenne?
fact: This ochre-trimmed cathedral anchors the center of French Guiana's capital. Its present form dates largely from the 19th century.

clue: Where is the Real Felipe Fortress?
fact: Spain built this star-shaped fortress to defend the port of Callao after the devastating 1746 earthquake and tsunami. It later played roles in Peru's independence wars.

clue: Where is Fuerte Bulnes?
fact: Chile established this wooden fort in 1843 to assert control over the Strait of Magellan. Harsh conditions soon prompted settlers to move to Punta Arenas.

clue: Where is the moai quarry at Rano Raraku?
fact: Nearly all Easter Island moai were carved from volcanic tuff at this crater. Hundreds remain standing, lying, or partly cut from bedrock.

clue: Where is the canopy tower near Tambopata Research Center?
fact: The tower gives researchers and visitors a treetop perspective on Peru's Amazon rainforest. Macaws gather at nearby clay licks.

clue: Where is the main boardwalk at El Tatio?
fact: Steam columns are most visible around dawn at this high Andean geothermal field. The site stands more than 4,300 meters above sea level.

clue: Where is the Goose Green memorial?
fact: The settlement was the scene of a major 1982 Falklands War battle. Memorials commemorate those killed in the fighting.

clue: Where is the Camp de la Transportation?
fact: Prisoners arriving in French Guiana were processed at this penal camp in Saint-Laurent-du-Maroni. Preserved cell blocks recall the transportation era.

clue: Where is Fort Nieuw Amsterdam in Suriname?
fact: This open-air museum occupies an 18th-century fort at the meeting of the Suriname and Commewijne rivers. Its earthworks guarded plantations and shipping.

clue: Where is Chacaltaya Cosmic Physics Observatory?
fact: This exceptionally high Bolivian research station studies cosmic rays and atmospheric physics. A nearby glacier and ski area largely vanished in recent decades.

clue: Where is Piedra del Cocuy?
fact: This isolated granite dome rises above Amazon forest near the meeting of Venezuela, Colombia, and Brazil. It is a striking navigation landmark along the Rio Negro region.

clue: Where is Times Square?
fact: Times Square is known for its bright lights, Broadway theaters, and New Year's Eve celebration.

clue: Where is the Louvre?
fact: The Louvre is the world's largest art museum and a historic monument in Paris.

clue: Where is Buckingham Palace?
fact: Buckingham Palace is the London residence and administrative headquarters of the British monarch.

clue: Where is the Burj Khalifa?
fact: At 828 meters, the Burj Khalifa is the world's tallest building.

clue: Where is Tokyo Tower?
fact: Tokyo Tower is a communications and observation tower inspired by the Eiffel Tower.

clue: Where is Red Square?
fact: Red Square is Moscow's historic heart, home to St. Basil's Cathedral and the Kremlin.

clue: Where is Tower Bridge?
fact: Tower Bridge is a combined bascule and suspension bridge over the River Thames in London.

clue: Where is Notre-Dame?
fact: Notre-Dame de Paris is a medieval Catholic cathedral on the Île de la Cité.

clue: Where is the Sistine Chapel?
fact: The Sistine Chapel is famous for Michelangelo's ceiling frescoes in Vatican City.

clue: Where is the Hollywood Sign?
fact: The Hollywood Sign overlooks Los Angeles from Mount Lee in Griffith Park.

clue: Where is the CN Tower?
fact: The CN Tower was the world's tallest freestanding structure from 1975 to 2007.

clue: Where is the Trevi Fountain?
fact: The Trevi Fountain is Rome's largest Baroque fountain and a popular tourist spot.

clue: Where is Shibuya Crossing?
fact: Shibuya Crossing is one of the world's busiest pedestrian intersections in Tokyo.

clue: Where is the Arc de Triomphe?
fact: The Arc de Triomphe honors those who fought and died for France in the French Revolution and Napoleonic Wars.

clue: Where is the Guggenheim Bilbao?
fact: The Guggenheim Museum Bilbao is renowned for its innovative titanium-clad architecture.

clue: Where is the Kaaba?
fact: The Kaaba in Mecca is Islam's holiest site and the direction of Muslim prayer.

clue: Where is the Temple of Heaven?
fact: The Temple of Heaven in Beijing was where emperors prayed for good harvests.

clue: Where is the Western Wall?
fact: The Western Wall is the last remaining wall of the Second Temple in Jerusalem.

clue: Where is the Taj-ul-Masjid?
fact: Taj-ul-Masjid is one of the largest mosques in India, located in Bhopal.

clue: Where is the Rock of Gibraltar?
fact: The Rock of Gibraltar is a monolithic limestone promontory at the entrance to the Mediterranean.

clue: Where are the Easter Island Moai?
fact: The Moai are monolithic statues created by the Rapa Nui people on Easter Island.

clue: Where is the U.S. Capitol?
fact: The U.S. Capitol is the home of the United States Congress in Washington, D.C.

clue: Where is the Kremlin?
fact: The Moscow Kremlin is a fortified complex that serves as the official residence of Russia's president.

clue: Where is the Panathenaic Stadium?
fact: The Panathenaic Stadium hosted the first modern Olympic Games in 1896.

clue: Where is the Florence Cathedral?
fact: The Duomo in Florence features Brunelleschi's revolutionary dome.

clue: Where is Milan Cathedral?
fact: Milan Cathedral is the largest Gothic cathedral in Italy.

clue: Where is St. Mark's Square?
fact: Piazza San Marco is Venice's main public square, known for St. Mark's Basilica.

clue: Where is Pisa Cathedral?
fact: Pisa Cathedral stands in the Piazza dei Miracoli alongside the Leaning Tower.

clue: Where is the Palace of Westminster?
fact: The Palace of Westminster houses the UK Parliament and Big Ben.

clue: Where is the Champs-Élysées?
fact: The Champs-Élysées is one of the world's most famous avenues in Paris.

clue: Where is the Louvre Pyramid?
fact: I.M. Pei's glass pyramid serves as the main entrance to the Louvre Museum.

clue: Where is Lalbagh Fort?
fact: Lalbagh Fort is an incomplete 17th-century Mughal fort complex in Dhaka.

clue: Where is the Merlion?
fact: The Merlion is Singapore's iconic statue with a lion's head and fish body.

clue: Where is the Fuji TV Building?
fact: The Fuji TV Building in Odaiba is known for its distinctive spherical observation deck.

clue: Where is Odaiba?
fact: Odaiba is a major entertainment district on a man-made island in Tokyo Bay.

clue: Where is the KL Tower?
fact: The KL Tower is a telecommunications tower and observation point in Kuala Lumpur.

clue: Where is the Texas State Capitol?
fact: The Texas State Capitol in Austin is one of the largest state capitol buildings in the U.S.

clue: Where is Cathedral of Our Lady located in Belgium?
fact: Famous Gothic cathedral with Rubens artworks.

clue: Where is Grand Place located in Belgium?
fact: UNESCO World Heritage square with ornate guildhalls.

clue: Where is Edinburgh Castle located in Scotland?
fact: Historic fortress on Castle Rock.

clue: Where is York Minster located in UK?
fact: Largest medieval Gothic cathedral in Northern Europe.

clue: Where is Canterbury Cathedral located in UK?
fact: Site of Thomas Becket's martyrdom.

clue: Where is Windsor Castle located in UK?
fact: Oldest and largest occupied castle in the world.

clue: Where is Dublin Castle located in Ireland?
fact: Historic castle complex in city center.

clue: Where is Amsterdam Canals located in Netherlands?
fact: UNESCO-listed canal ring from the Golden Age.

clue: Where is the Dom Tower, the soaring Gothic landmark separated from its cathedral by a storm?
fact: Tallest church tower in the Netherlands.

clue: Where is Port of Rotterdam located in Netherlands?
fact: Europe's largest seaport.

clue: Where is Krakow Old Town located in Poland?
fact: UNESCO medieval old town square.

clue: Where is Tallinn Old Town located in Estonia?

clue: Where is Riga Old Town located in Latvia?

clue: Where is Vilnius Old Town located in Lithuania?

clue: Where is Gdansk Old Town located in Poland?
